title: White rock performers copying Black artists: Joplin, Bessie Smith, Mae West
summary: Johnston describes rock performers listening to Bessie Smith and Gil adds that Mae West built an act on Bessie Smith.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: When I first met Janis Joplin I sat in what was its Fillmore East, and heard her doing an exact copy of something that I had heard before. An exact copy.
Oh a lot of rock groups have done that.

Oh yes. Of course they stay here and I know that I don't even recall the name of the group now. But it was one of the most famous of the rock groups and I was invited to their apartment one afternoon to talk and when I walked in they were sitting there listening to Bessie Smith and had been listening to Bessie Smith for hours.
Well Mae West made a living of what she picked up off of Bessie Smith. Her style and all that kind of stuff. Mae West really picked that up and parlayed it into something.
And next door at this little record shop the man over there used to tell me all of

the records that the white musicians who were living in this hotel were buying. That's right. And I have a number of them right there in that cabinet. Because I then would get them to see what they were listening to. (LAUGHTER). And what their influences were.
Some few acknowledged some of the major ones but I've been here long enough, as I've said I've been here six years and I certainly know that they sit for hours and listen to these black performers.
